archetypes.name: kv-contract
archetypes.rationale: The plan defines explicit KV allowlists for two driver result-envs and two parallel handoff loops in SKILL.md; misalignment between emitted keys, allowed keys, and consumed keys is the primary silent-failure vector for this refactor.
archetypes.prompt_body: Cross-check the plan's stated emit allowlists for design-route.sh and design-init-runparams.sh against the SKILL.md orchestrator handoff fences: every key the driver is specified to emit must appear in the orchestrator's allowlisted read loop, and every key the orchestrator reads must be in the driver's emit list. Check that WARN and ERROR lines are handled consistently — the plan says they are printed as breadcrumbs rather than stored via printf -v, but verify this rule is stated the same way in both the SKILL.md update spec and the .md sibling contract. Verify the resume@<STEP> KV re-export list (RESUME_STEP, SESSION_ID, RUN_ID, TIER, BRAINSTORM_DONE) is fully covered by the design-route.sh allowlist. Check for any keys mentioned in edge-case descriptions or failure-mode mitigations that are absent from the allowlists. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: bash32-portability
archetypes.rationale: Repository scripts must target Bash 3.2 and the Renderer Substitution Safety rule applies to template replacements; the plan's jq invocation, mktemp patterns, and ${REPO:+} expansion shapes are not explicitly verified for portability.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review every code construct or pseudo-code in the plan for Bash 4+ features forbidden in this repository: associative arrays (declare -A), namerefs (declare -n/local -n), mapfile/readarray, parameter case conversion (${var^^}), append-all redirection (&>>), and coprocs. Check the plan's jq invocation pattern — specifically the --argjson flag usage and the canonical filter string — for any shell-quoting shape requiring three or more levels of nesting that would violate the BASH_AUTHORING.md file-backed-script rule. Examine the plan's mktemp temp-file pattern and the mv-over-run-params.json atomic-replace step for portability differences between macOS BSD mktemp and GNU mktemp. Verify that the plan's ${REPO:+--repo "$REPO"} conditional expansion is safe under the Renderer Substitution Safety rule when OWNER/REPO names contain an ampersand or other special characters. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
